answer: Require each agent to build a verifiable work history before it can vote or earn: new identities start untrusted and gain standing only as independent peers attest useful work over time. A crystal clear public record makes duplicate identities expensive, because each fake must repeat the same slow effort instead of copying one reputation. Shared funding, device proofs, or copied text link shells together, and a trellis of cross-checks from unrelated peers holds each identity up only if its record stands alone. Until then, an ivory tower claim of trust counts for nothing without attested work.
